Yunnan is a province in southwest province of the People's Republic of China. The area of Yunnan Province is 394100 km2. It spans approximately 394,000 square kilometres (152,000 sq mi) and has a population of 47.2 million (as of 2020). The capital of the province is Kunming. The province borders Vietnam, Laos and Burma. Yunnan Province is divided into eight municipalities (地级市) and eight autonomous prefectures (自治州). Kunming Municipality (昆明市) - Provincial capital Yunnan's cultural life is one of remarkable diversity. It is famous for ethnic minority groups, Yuanmou Human archaeological findings, ancient Tea Horse Road legends, Puer teas and Yunnan Baiyao medicines. Dali, the historic center of the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms. Chuxiong, the first stop on the way to Dali and Lijiang. Home of the Yi ethnic minority and their respective ancient town. Jinghong, the center and prefectural capital of the Xishuangbanna Dai minority autonomous prefecture. Lijiang, a Naxi minority city. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997. Xamgyi'nyilha County (also known as Shangri-La and formerly Zhongdian), an ethnic Tibetan township and county set high in Yunnan's northwestern mountains. Shilin (Stone Forest), a series of karst outcrops east of Kunming. Yuanyang, a Hani minority settlement with vast rice-terraced mountains. Xishuangbanna, a national scenic resort, noted for its natural and cultural attractions.

Yunyarinyi is an Aboriginal community on the Aṉangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara Lands in South Australia. It is about 45 km south of the border with the Northern Territory, and 320 km south of Alice Springs. It is 40 km from the larger community of Pukatja, where most of the services are located. Yunyarinyi started as a cattle station called Kenmore Park. It officially became an indigenous community when the land rights were granted in 1981. Today, Yunyarinyi has a school, a community centre with a shared kitchen, a community office and a local garage (repair shop). The number of people living at Yunyarinyi is about 40 to 45; many of them are children.

Yunusemre (former name: Saru) is a neighbourhood of the municipality and district of Mihalıççık, Eskişehir Province, Turkey. It is named after the great Turkish poet Yunus Emre (1238–1320) whose tomb is in the town. Yunusemre is situated along the Porsuk River and the railroad connecting Ankara to Istanbul. It is 100 kilometres (62 mi) east of Eskişehir.

Yungngora is an Aboriginal community in the Kimberley region of Western Australia. It is located on the banks of the Fitzroy River. Yungngora is about 280 kilometers east-south-east of Broome and about 100 kilometers southwest of Fitzroy Crossing. The community is home to people from different language groups, including the Nyikina and Walmajarri people. Yungngora's name comes from a nearby billabong (a small lake that forms in a river). As of 2016, Yungngora had a population of 378. Yungngora was established in the late 1970s by elders who wanted to return to their traditional land. Many Aboriginal people who worked on cattle stations faced poor conditions and low wages. After the 1967 referendum, which aimed to improve Aboriginal rights, many people sought to reclaim their connection to their land. The land where Yungngora is located was once part of Noonkanbah Station. In 1976, the Noonkanbah pastoral lease was bought for the community. This was a significant step towards self-determination and cultural revival for the Yungngora people. In April 2007, the Yungngora people had their native title recognized, affirming their rights to the land. Yungngora has a population of around 378 people in 2016. The main languages spoken are Kriol, Walmajarri, Nyikina, and English. Many children attend Kulkarriya Community School, where English is often a second or third language. Yungngora has essential services for its residents: Kulkarriya Community School: Provides education for primary and secondary students. Health Clinic: Offers medical services. Health and Aged Care (HAAC) kitchen and office: Provides meals for the elderly. Community Store: Sells food and other necessities. Airstrip: For transport to and from the community. Recreation: Includes basketball courts and a football oval.

Yushan, also called Mount Jade and Mount Yu is a mountain in Taiwan. It is the tallest mountain in Taiwan because it is 3952 m above sea level. The mountain used to be called Mount Morrison, but it isn't called that anymore. That name was named after Robert Morrison, who is a missionary. The mountain is usually called Yushan or Mount Jade. In the winter, the top of Yushan usually has a lot of thick snow. The snow makes the top shine like jade. That is why it is called Mount Jade. Yushan and all the mountains around it are part of the Yushan Range of mountains. The Yushan Range is in Yushan National Park. The area has the largest amount of natural space that has not been developed. It has a lot of forests and many types of animals.

Yuxia Railway Station is in Yuxia, Huyi, Xi'an. It is a Railway Station on Xi'an-Yuxia Railway. In November 1955, it opened and started using during Chinese First five-year plan. On October 21, 2000, it stopped carrying passengers. Then it only carried goods.

Yōmei Seamount is an underwater volcano (seamount) of the Hawaiian–Emperor seamount chain in the Pacific Ocean. Yōmei is an extinct volcano. This seabed mountain is named after Emperor Yōmei of Japan. The last eruption from Yōmei seamount was between 60 million and 65 million years ago.

Yüksekova is a city and a district of Hakkari Province of southeastern Turkey. It is located very close to the borders with both Iraq and Iran. In February of 2020 it was buried under 6 meters of snow. The city and district is populated entirely by Kurds.

Zabul is a historic province in southern Afghanistan. Qalat is the capital. About 275,100 people live in the province. The major ethnic group is Pashtun. Zabul is surrounded by Paktika and Ghzani provinces in the east, Urozgan province in the north, Kandahar province in west and southwest, and Balochistan state of Pakistan in south. Around 800,000 people live in Zabul. Most of them live in Shahjoi, Arghandab and Kalat city. Almond, grapes, apricots, wheat, and vegetables are the main agricultural products of Zabul. About 80% of the people are farmers. The current governor of Zabul province is Bissmillah Afghanmal, son of Haji Mauladad Momand, born in Kandahar in 1976. In 2006, the province's first airstrip was opened near Qalat. It was for the Afghan National Army. The airstrip is not paved.
Zahedshahr (; formerly, Zahedan, also Romanized as Zāhedān and Zāhidān) is a city and capital of Shibkaveh District, in Fasa County, Fars Province, Iran.

Zahedan is a city in Iran. It is the capital of Sistan and Baluchestan Province in Southeastern Iran. As of 2016, Zahedan has over 600,000 people. the city is near the borderlands between Iran and Pakistan where Baloch people live. The demographics of the inhabiants of Zahedan are mixed with Balochis, and Persians. They speak Persian and Balochi. Zahedan is east of the Dasht-e Loot. Zahedan is part of Baluchestan, a historic region of Asia. Sunni Muslims live in Zahedan as well. Shaikh Abdolhamid Ismaeelzahi is the main and most influential religious and Sunni and the Baloch people. Zahedan is located in the southeastern part of Iran. It is 1,491 kilometers southeast of Tehran, 950 kilometers south of Mashhad, 1,189 kilometers southeast of Isfahan, 2,024 kilometers southeast of Tabriz, and 95 kilometers from the Iran-Pakistan border. It is also connected by rail to Pakistan and is near to Afghanistan. Zahedan is the Iranian city, which is the closest to Afghanistan and Pakistan. As of 2016, Zahedan has 587,730 people. In the 1930s, Zahedan was a small village. In 1930, Zahedan's population reached 17,500. and increased more than fivefold to 93,000 by 1976. After 1980, large numbers of Iranians fleeing the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan helped triple the population of Zahedan to more than 281,000 by 1986, a number which has since doubled again.

The Zambezi River is the fourth largest river in Africa. It is also the largest river that enters the Indian Ocean. It starts in Zambia, flows successively through Angola, Zambia again, borders Namibia, Botswana and Zimbabwe, through Mozambique where it enters the ocean. Much more water flows during the rainy season, October through March. The Victoria Falls, the most beautiful sight on the river, is listed as one of the UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The Kariba Dam on the Zambezi is a major source of hydroelectricity

Zalzala Koh or Zalzala Jazeera, meaning "Earthquake Island", is a small island off the coast of the port city of Gwadar, Balochistan in south east of Pakistan. The island appeared on 24 September 2013, following an earthquake. It is believed to have been made by a mud volcano, where gas pushed up soil and mud from under the sea. The round island is about 15 m high and between 70 m and 90 m across. Gas is still escaping from cracks in the surface. Scientists believe that the island will not last for very long. Within months the level of the island had dropped by more than two metres, and it appears to be sinking backing into the sea.

Zamboanga City (Chavacano: Ciudad de Zamboanga; ) is a city in Mindanao, Phillippines. It is the sixth-largest city of the Phillippines. Zamboanga City is called the "Sardines Capital of the Philippines". This is because 9 of the 12 sardine companies in the country are in the city. Other names for the city are "Asia's Latin City" and "City of Flowers". The city of Zamboanga is politically divided into 98 barangays or barrios. Many landmarks are in the city. These include:

Zamboanga Peninsula is an administrative region in the Philippines. It is also known as Region IX. The regional center is Pagadian. The region has three provinces (Zamboanga del Norte, Zamboanga Sibugay and Zamboanga del Sur) and two cities (Isabela City and Zamboanga City). In September 9, 2024 the province of Sulu is including in the region.

Zamboanga del Sur, officially the Province of Zamboanga del Sur, is a province in the Philippines. It is in the Zamboanga Peninsula region in Mindanao. Its capital is the city of Pagadian. It is grouped with the very urbanized City of Zamboanga but the two are geographically separated from each other. The city also has its own government. The province borders Zamboanga del Norte to the north, Zamboanga Sibugay to the west, Misamis Occidental to the northeast, and Lanao del Norte to the east. To the south is the Moro Gulf.

Zaranj or Zarang is the capital of Nimruz Province in south-western Afghanistan. There are about 49,851 people in the city. It is next to Milak, Iran. It is linked by highways with Lashkar Gah to the east, Farah to the north and Zabol in Iran to the west.
Zarrineh is a city in the Kurdistan province of Iran. Its people speak Kurdish. They are followers of Islam. At the 2006 census, its population was 1,272, in 266 families.

Zarqan County is a county in Fars Province, Iran. At the 2006 census, its population was 46,672, in 11,815 families. The county has two cities: Zarqan and Lapui. The county has three rural districts (dehestan): Band-e Amir Rural District, Rahmatabad Rural District, and Zarqan Rural District. The Zarqan County was established on 2018 in Fars province.
Zarqan (, also Romanized as Zarqān; also known as Zarghanak and Zargān) is a city and capital of Zarqan District, in Shiraz County, Fars Province, Iran.

Zaw Htay (, also known as Hmuu Zaw; died 23 May 2022) was a spokesman of the Myanmar government who was the director general of the State Counsellor's Office from April 2016 to February 2021. He was the presidential spokesman of the Myanmar Office of the President from April 2011 to April 2016 under President Thein Sein.

The Zarafshon is a river in Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, Central Asia. Its name, "spreader of gold" in Persian, refers to the presence of gold-bearing sands in the upper reaches of the river. To the ancient Greeks it was known as the Polytimetus. It was also formerly known as Sughd River. The river is 877 kilometres (545 mi) long and has a basin area of 17,700 square kilometres (6,800 sq mi). A part of the river valley is known to the Kyrgyz people as Raskam, and the river itself is also called the Raskam River. The river is also known as the Zarafshan River. The area was once claimed by the ruler of Hunza.

Zhanaozen is a city in the Mangystau Region of Kazakhstan. As of 2023, 74,357 people live here, and 147,933 people live in the urban area. The city was founded in 1964 after oil was discovered nearby.

Zhejiang is a province in east China. "Zhejiang" is named by the Qiantang River, which is also called "Zhejiang". "Zhejiang" means "bent river". It has a population of more than 64 million people. The capital of Zhejiang Province is Hangzhou. Zhejiang Province is divided into eleven municipalities (Chinese:地级市).

Zhanjiang, is a prefecture-level city at the southwestern end of Guangdong province, People's Republic of China, facing Hainan to the south. Its population was 6,994,832 inhabitants at the 2010 census. 1,611,868 live in the built-up area made of four urban districts: Chikan, Xiashan, Potou and Mazhang. In 2007, the city is named China's top ten livable cities by Chinese Cities Brand Value Report, which was released at 2007 Beijing Summit of China Cities Forum.

Zhob is a district in the northwest of Balochistan province of Pakistan. The Zhob district is a Provincially Administered Tribal Area (PATA). The Zhob district is subdivided into three subdistricts: Zhob, Kakkar and Sherani. The population of Zhob district was estimated to be over 500,000 in 2005. The Zhob River is used for irrigation in the Zhob district.

Zhengzhou (, pinyin: zhèngzhōu) is the capital of Henan Province in the People's Republic of China. It is in the northcentral part of Henan. Zhengzhou is on the southern bank of the Yellow River. It is one of the Eight Great Ancient Capitals of China. In 2010, 9,378,000 people lived there. As of 2017, the prefecture-level city is divided into 6 urban districts, 5 county-level cities and 1 county. Because of rapid population growth, the subdivisions may change.

Zhongli District is a district in Taoyuan City, Taiwan. Zhongli is spelled variously as Jungli, Jongli, Jhongli or Chungli on railway, bus stop and road signs. Historically, the city is the site of the Jungli Incident of 1977, the most significant event of the democratization movement prior to the 1980s. Ethnically, it is considered a kind of capital city for the Hakka Taiwanese, who live in great numbers here and nearby; a lot of the elderly could speak Hakka in addition to Mandarin and Taiwanese Hokkien. Recently many foreign workers (mainly from the Philippines and Thailand) have also settled in and around the city because of the heavy industries in the suburbs of the city. It is a center for foreign laborers. The city of Zhongli has 3 large parks and over 70 green reserves in the city for residents of Zhongli to enjoy.
Zhetisay is a city in the Turkistan Region of Kazakhstan. There are 45,130 people living there (as of 2023). It was founded in 1939. It was given city status in 1969.

Zhitikara (,, until 1997 - Dzhetygara ) is a single-industry town, the administrative center of the Zhitikara district of the Kostanay region of the Republic of Kazakhstan. It is located on the Shortandy River. As of 2023, 35,298 people live here and 42,611 people live in the urban area. The city is home to the largest and only enterprise for the extraction and enrichment of chrysotile asbestos called Kostanay Minerals in Kazakhstan The city of Zhitikara is located in the southwestern part of the Kostanay region near the Kazakh-Russian border, 217 kilometers from the regional center of the city of Kostanay. The territory of the city occupies an area of 6080 hectares, the height above sea level is 271 m.

Zhouzhi County (, pinyin:Zhōuzhì Xiàn) is a county of Xi'an, Shaanxi, China. It is in the southwest part of Xi'an. Before 1964, it was written in Chinese as 盩厔 (also read Zhouzhi), meaning surrounded by mountains and rivers. It covers 2945.20 km2. As of November 2010, 562,768 people lived there. Zhouzhi is famous for embroidery, and the product kiwifruit.

Zhuhai is a city in Guangdong, China. It is in the Pearl River Delta. It borders Jiangmen to the northwest, Zhongshan to the north, and Macau to the south. Zhuhai was one of the original Special Economic Zones established in the 1980s. Zhuhai is one of China's popular tourist destinations, being called the Chinese Riviera. Most people in the city are migrants who speak Mandarin. Its northern part, Xiangzhou district is now part of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen built-up area, the biggest built-up area in the world. The area had more than 44,478,513 people in 2010. It includes Shenzhen, Dongguan, Foshan, Zhongshan, Macao, the main part of Guangzhou, and small parts of Jiangmen and Huizhou.
Zhoukou is a prefecture-level city in eastern Henan province, China. In 2010, 8,953,793 people lived there. Zhoukou administers 1 district, 1 county-level city and 8 counties.

Zhumadian (驻马店) is a prefecture-level city in southern Henan in the People's Republic of China. It has also been spelled Chumatien. In 2010, 7,230,744 people lived there. Zhumadian administers 1 district and 9 counties.

Zi Yu (Chinese: 梓渝; born 6 July 2002), also known by his real name Zheng Peng (Chinese: 郑朋), is a Chinese singer and actor. He was a student at the Department of Performing Arts at the Beijing Contemporary Music Academy (Chinese: 北京现代音乐研修学院). Born in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, in 2002, Zi Yu attended the Beijing Contemporary Music Academy. There, he was discovered by a talent scout. On May 28, 2019, he became a trainee with the entertainment company Huakai Banxia (Chinese: 花开半夏). On June 26, 2020, he appeared as a Huakai Banxia trainee in "We Are Young" (Chinese: 少年之名), a Youku's boy band survival program. On September 19, 2020, he appeared on "Emperor Has Arrived" (Chinese: 欧皇驾到), a Youku's fashion toy variety show. In January 2021, Zi Yu again competed as a Huakai Banxia trainee in iQiyi's boy band survival show, "Youth With You Season Three." But he did not get a spot in the final group. In February 2021, he appeared in "Youth in Bloom" (Chinese: 花开的少年们), an iQiyi's game challenge mini-variety show. On June 25, 2021, he joined the boy band Guanghe Shaonian and made his formal debut. His acting career began on August 25, 2022. He played the role of Xiao Ban (Chinese: 萧绊) in his first TV series, "My Lady General" (Chinese: 将军在下). On December 8, 2022, word went that he had been bullied by the band's leader, Zheng Xingyuan, for a long period. On December 10, the company denied the bully claims. Later, a voice recording of Zi Yu comforting his fans was shared online. By December 23, Zi Yu had started talks with Huakai Banxia to end his contract. On January 8, 2023, the company asked him to pack his things and move to Hangzhou by January 14. On January 9, Zi Yu said he had been bullied by Zheng Xingyuan and claimed he would take legal action to end his contract. After Zi Yu's post spread online, Zheng Xingyuan said that an argument during practice had become a physical fight. He also showed a medical certificate and said he had depression. Fans called his certificate "a fake" because his medical check only took one minute. Although Zi Yu was able to end his contract, he had to pay a fine of 600,000 Chinese yuan within five years. This caused financial problems, and he took many part-time jobs to make money. In June 2025, the TV series "Revenged Love" (Chinese: 逆爱) was released, and Zi Yu became famous.
Ziarat is a valley located in Lower Chitral District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province of Pakistan. Its coordinates are 35° 40' 26" North, 71° 55' 28" East.
Zibo is a prefecture-level city in central Shandong province, China. In 2020, 4,704,138 people lived there. Zibo administers five districts and three counties:

Zoji La is a high mountain pass in India. This pass is 13000 ft above sea level, at 74.50 longitude and 34.17 latitude. The pass connects a valley of Kashmir with Ladakh. Different trade routes lad to Tibet, China and Central Asia. Renchen Shah of Leh entered Kashmir through this pass and became the monarch of the land in the 14th century. Mirza Haider Doughlat also advanced through this pass to invade Kashmir. The old historical name of the pass was Shurji La meaning lord Shiva's mountain.

Çorlu is a city in Turkey. It is located in the province of Tekirdağ at East Thrace. The land around Çorlu is mostly flat. Çorlu is located at a height. There are about 111 people per square kilometer. Çorlu is quite densely populated. Çorlu is the largest town in the area. The area around Çorlu is almost covered in fields. The climate is Mediterranean. The average temperature is 14 °C. The warmest month is July, at 27 °C, and the coldest is December, at 4 °C. The average rainfall is 892 millimeters per year. The wettest month is December, with 128 millimeters of rain, and the driest is July, with 17 millimeters.

Çanakkale Province is a province of Turkey in the Marmara Region. It takes its name from the city of Çanakkale. Like Istanbul, Çanakkale province has a European (Thrace) and an Asian (Anatolia) part. The European part is the Gallipoli (Gelibolu) peninsula. The Asian part is mostly the historic region of Troad in Anatolia. The Dardanelles strait is between them. It connects the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean Sea. The archaeological site of Troy is thought to be in Çanakkale province. Çanakkale is the biggest district of the province. The European and Asian parts of the province were connected to each other with the completion of the Çanakkale 1915 Bridge in March 2022.

Üsküdar is a district of Istanbul, Turkey, located in the Anatolian part of the city in a neighboring valley on the banks of the Bosporus, being its ancient name Chrysopolis (golden city), and in the mediaeval period Scutari.

Đồng Hới is the capital city of Quảng Bình Province, in the north central coast of Vietnam. The city's area is 155.54 km² (60 square miles). In 2005, 103,005 people lived there. It is at around 500 km (310 mi) south of Hà Nội (Hanoi), 260 km (160 mi) north of Đà Nẵng (Danang), 1,200 km (750 mi) north of Hồ Chí Minh City (Saigon). It borders Laos on the west, the South China Sea on the east, Hà Tĩnh province on the north, and Quảng Ninh in the south. Dong Hoi Airport is 6 km north of Dong Hoi. The city was close to the Vietnamese DMZ, and it was in North Vietnam during the Vietnam War. Since it was so close to the DMZ, it was important for the North Vietnamese. For this reason, the city was heavily bombed by the US Air Force. There is a cathedral called the Tam Toa Church that was bombed during the war. Tam Toa is still ruined today so people could remember the bombing of North Vietnam. Dong Hoi is subdivided into 16 subdivisions, 10 urban wards (phường) and 6 rural communes (xã).

İzmir is a city in the west of Turkey. It has one of the biggest seaports in the Aegean Sea region and all of Turkey. İzmir is a popular destination for tourists, who come for beaches and cultural tours in the region. It has a hot-summer Mediterranean climate (Csa in the Köppen climate classification). İzmir is the third largest city in Turkey. This is an ancient city; many scholars think Homer was born in Smyrna. Earthquakes destroyed the city in 187 AD, 1653, 1688, 1739, and 1778, and it was rebuilt many times. The last big earthquake was in 2020, which caused more than 117 deaths and the collapse of 8 buildings. The Greek name for this formerly Greek city is Smyrna, from which the Turkish name İzmir comes. The Greek name was also used in English until the early 20th century. About 30 km (20 miles) south of İzmir, there is an ancient Greek city named Ephesus. İzmir was a candidate for Expo 2015. However, Milan had more support, so İzmir lost.
Kocaeli is a city in northwestern Turkey. The city is in the Marmara Region. In 2013, 1,676,202 people lived there. The city was badly damaged and many people died in the 1999 İzmit earthquake.

Ōakura is a small township in the Taranaki Region of New Zealand's North Island. It is located 15 kilometers south-west of New Plymouth on State Highway 45. Ōkato is 12 kilometers further south-west. It was hit by a tornado in July 2007.

İzmir Province is a province and metropolitan municipality of Turkey in the Aegean Region, situated along the Aegean coast. Its capital is the city of İzmir, which has 11 districts out of 30 in total. To the west, it is surrounded by the Aegean Sea, and it encloses the Gulf of Izmir. Its area is 11,973 square kilometres (4,623 square miles), with a population of 4,425,789 in 2021. The population was 3,370,866 in 2000. Neighboring provinces are Balıkesir to the north, Manisa to the east, and Aydın to the south.
Ōakura is a small coastal settlement in the Whangarei District, New Zealand. It is situated 48 kilometers northerneast of Whangārei on State Highway 1. Its nearby school is in Whangaruru.

Ōsaka Station (大阪駅,おおさかえき) is a railway station of JR West in Kita-ku, Osaka, Japan. This station is also connected to Umeda Station. Ōkuma is a Japanese town in Fukushima Prefecture on the island of Honshu. The latitude is 37°22'19" ~ 37°25'50" N and the longitude is 140°51'29" ~ 141°2'30" E. In 2003, the estimated population was 10,945, with a population density of 139.07 inhabitants per km². The total area is 78.70 km². The Fukushima Nuclear Power Plant No. 1 is located in the city where a series of nuclear accidents occurred in 2011. As of May 1, 2023, the city had 10,004 inhabitants in 4,852 households. However, this figure is significantly higher than the actual number, as the municipality continues to keep records of residents despite evacuations to settlements elsewhere in the country. The city's actual population was 545 in May 2023 and 1,052 as of August 4, 2025. There are three towns, one village, one city, and one district next to Ōkuma. Ōkuma is located on the Pacific Ocean coast, in the central part of Fukushima. Ōkuma is located in the center of the Hamadōri region of Fukushima, bordering the Abukuma Highlands to the west and the Pacific Ocean to the east. It lies between the cities of Namie and Futaba to the north, Tamura to the west, and Kawauchi and Tomioka to the south. The city is home to the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant. Within the city limits is Mount Higakure (日隠山, Higakure-yama), with an elevation of 601.5 m above sea level. The Kuma River (熊川, Kuma-gawa) also flows through the city. The city is bordered to the east by the Pacific Ocean, to the west by the city of Miyakoji in Tamura Ward near the Abukuma Mountains, to the south by the cities of Tomioka and Kawauchi, and to the north by Namie and Futaba. Tren is high in the west and low in the east, with an altitude ranging from 695 to 3 m above sea level. It covers an area of 15.4 km from east to west and 6.7 km from north to south. Mountains and forests cover 65% of the total area, of which approximately 50% is state-owned. The Abukuma Mountains extend toward the sea from three hills, to the south, center, and north of the city, respectively. Three rivers flow between them: the Kuma, Koirino, and Ottozawa to the east, with farmland in their basins. The terrain of Ōkuma Machi is mountainous in the west but flat in the east. The climate is oceanic, annual precipitation is about 1,200 mm, and there is almost no snow, even in winter. South: Iwaki (47 km), Mito (142 km). West: Kōriyama (77 km), Aizuwakamatsu (137 km) According to Japanese census data, Ōkuma's population grew steadily over the past 40 years until the nuclear disaster. From its name "Kuma" to the present day, Okuma has historically been a border area where northern and southern powers competed. Historically, Okuma is known as the northern gateway to the Kantō-Tohoku border area. During the Kuni no Miyatsuko period in the first half of the 7th century, present-day Okuma formed the northern boundary of Iwaki Kuni no Miyatsuko and the northern boundary of Taka Province and was called "Kuma Village". Furthermore, while Sukegawa (present-day Hitachi City in Ibaraki Prefecture) was called "Michinokuchi no Kihe", Kuma Village was called "Michinoshiri no Kihe". Taka Province was a regional state formed by the merger of the three regions of Taka Kuni no Miyatsuko, Kikuta no Miyatsuko, and Iwaki Kuni no Miyatsuko. This region has a geographical and historical identity, as in the first half of the 20th century it became an energy source region, along with the Hitachi mines and the Joban coal mines. With the establishment of the Ritsuryō system in the second half of the 7th century, Taka Province was incorporated into Hitachi Province, with Kuma Village as its northern boundary. However, in 718, in the early Nara period, the area north of Kikuta County, whose boundary is at present-day Nakoso (Hiragata Tunnel), was separated from Hitachi Province and incorporated into Sekishiro Province, which extended from Nakoso to Watari, with Kuma Village becoming the central village of Sekishiro Province. However, around 728, Sekishiro Province was incorporated into Mutsu Province. The village of Kuma, in the 7th century, was renamed Kumakawa, after the river that flows through the area, and this period lasted until the end of the Boshin War. From the founding of the Kamakura shogunate until the first half of the Sengoku period, Kumakawa became the territory of the Shireha clan and formed the southern border of their territory. However, in the second half of the Sengoku period, the Shireha clan was defeated by the Sōma clan. The Sōma clan's dominance lasted from the second half of the Sengoku period until the end of the Boshin War, and Kumakawa became the southern border of the Sōma clan's territory. The border between the Sōma and Iwaki clans during the Sengoku period, as well as the border between the Sōma-Nakamura and Iwaki-daira domains during the Edo period, was the town of Yonomori, located on the present-day border between the cities of Okuma and Tomioka. At the end of the Sengoku period, Kumakawa served as a buffer zone between the Sōma, Iwaki, and Tamura clans. When the Tamura Territory became a vassal domain of Date Masamune, who continued his expansion in defiance of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the Sōma clan, along with the Iwaki clan, moved west from Kumakawa to invade the Tamura Territory. This route is now known as National Highway 288. During the Edo period, during the Tokugawa shogunate, Kumagawa came under the control of the Nakamura dynasty, and a post town was established on Hama-kaido (now National Highway 6) and flourished as a post town called Kumagawa-juku. On September 22, 1868, Soma Nakamura Domain was defeated by Meiji government forces in the Boshin War. As a result, the former territory of Nakamura Domain, including Kumagawa, was transferred to Iwaki Prefecture. Following the abolition of feudal domains and the creation of prefectures on August 29, 1871, Kumagawa initially belonged to Nakamura Prefecture, but on January 9, 1872, Nakamura Prefecture and Taira Prefecture (formerly Iwaki Taira Domain) were merged to form Iwasaki Prefecture. On August 21, 1876, Iwasaki Prefecture was merged with Fukushima Prefecture (Nakadori) and Wakamatsu Prefecture (Aizu) and has been part of Fukushima Prefecture ever since. April 1, 1889: With the introduction of the town-village system, the villages of Ono and Kumamachi were established in Shioba County. April 1, 1896: Shioba and Naraha counties were merged to form Futaba County. November 22, 1904: Ono Station opened on the Joban Line. November 1, 1954: The towns of Oono and Kumamachi were merged to form the city of Okuma. As a result of rapid economic growth, the mining region stretching from Sukegawa (Hitachi City) to Yonomori (the Hitachi Mine and the Joban Coalfields of the early 20th century) declined. Oil and nuclear power began to replace coal as new energy sources. The Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant was built in Okuma. Construction of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant, owned by the Tokyo Electric Power Company, began in Okuma on September 29, 1967 (inauguration on March 26, 1971). Two days later, on October 1, 1967, the entire Joban Line was electrified, completing electrification between Taira Station (present-day Iwaki Station) and Iwanuma Station. Okuma thus became the northernmost "energy zone." Residents of the Yonomori region, including Okuma and Namie, who had previously moved to other areas for winter work when agriculture was unavailable, were now able to work year-round at the nuclear power plants. Nuclear power plants were considered "lucky gods" for residents, providing stable employment and significant subsidies. Following the opening of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant and the end of a period of rapid economic growth, "nuclear monaki" (a type of bean jam sandwich) bearing the image of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant were sold as souvenirs in Okuma. In 2006, the Ohno Hospital Incident symbolized the shortage of medical care and the problem of depopulation. The area was evacuated because of the Fukushima nuclear disaster in 2011. On March 11, 2011, the Great East Japan Earthquake struck Okuma, causing damage measuring over 6.0 on the Richter scale. The earthquake triggered a hydrogen explosion at Unit 1 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant at 3:36 p.m. on March 12. To avoid radiation exposure, residents were forced to evacuate beginning on March 13, with many moving to the Tamura Municipal Gymnasium in Funabiki, Funabiki-cho, Tamura City, Fukushima Prefecture, where a temporary town hall was set up. (Other evacuees and evacuation sites were also dispersed.) On March 14, at 11:01 a.m., a hydrogen explosion also occurred at Unit 3 of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant. After April 3, the temporary city hall and evacuated residents were relocated to the Aizuwakamatsu City Hall's Oitemachi Second Building in Sakaemachi, Aizuwakamatsu City, Fukushima Prefecture. On April 5, a branch office of the Aizuwakamatsu Municipal Office (jointly with the Okuma Welfare Board and the Okuma Chamber of Commerce and Industry) opened at the new location. In mid-April, an elementary school, a junior high school, and a kindergarten opened in Aizuwakamatsu. (The elementary school and kindergarten were branches of Okuma Elementary School and Okuma Kindergarten, which were formed by merging existing local schools and kindergartens, and the junior high school was a branch of an existing school.) Following the nuclear power plant accident, the town hall and residents were evacuated to nearby areas. From April 22, 2011, to December 9, 2012, the area was designated as a restricted access zone, with entry prohibited to all residents except workers performing decontamination, debris removal, and repair work. At midnight on December 10, 2012, the area was transformed into a "no return zone" (where entry and temporary return of residents other than workers is, as before, prohibited; however, temporary return (without overnight stays) may be permitted during the day, on designated days or by appointment; this corresponds to the former residence of 96% of the total population), a "restricted stay zone" and an "evacuation preparation zone" (where temporary entry and return during the day are only permitted with the authorization of the city council, but overnight stays are not permitted; in total, this corresponds to the former residence of 4% of the total population). The evacuation orders for the "restricted stay zone" and the "evacuation preparation zone" were lifted at midnight on April 10, 2019. The evacuation order for the "difficult return zone" around Ono Station was also lifted at midnight on March 5, 2020. At 9:00 a.m. on March 8, 2021, additional areas were opened to the public, and on November 30, 2021, the entire "Designated Base Area for Recovery and Revitalization" was opened to the public at 9:00 a.m. On June 30, 2022, the evacuation order for the entire "Designated Base Recovery and Revitalization Area" was lifted. According to the New York Times in 2013, the people of Ōkuma, like many other communities in Fukushima, are "starting to come to terms with a sobering realization: their old homes are probably lost forever, and they must start anew elsewhere." The people who used to live in Ōkuma are called "nuclear refugees". Between 2013 and 2019, six men in their 60s, working as temporary municipal employees, formed the so-called "Elderly Squad" and patrolled the city from the local government liaison office near the Sakashita Dam in the western part of the city. The Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant is currently being decommissioned. Following the nuclear disaster, the city is striving to transform itself into a city powered by renewable energy sources. On January 18, 2024, a decarbonization collaboration agreement was signed, involving the transmission of electricity generated from solar energy and other sources to Tokyo's Chuo Ward and the absorption of carbon dioxide in local forests. In 2024, the company signed a reconstruction cooperation agreement with the Ritsumeikan Trust, which manages Ritsumeikan University and other institutions. Ōkuma has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification Cfa). The average annual temperature in Ōkuma is 12.1°C (53.8°F). The average annual rainfall is 1,329 mm (52.3 in), with September being the wettest month. The highest temperature is reached in August, at around 24.1°C (75.4°F), and the lowest in January, at around 1.5°C (34.7°F). Ōkuma has three public elementary schools, one municipal public junior high school, and one public high school operated by the Fukushima Prefectural Board of Education. Classes at all schools remain indefinitely suspended. Due to the evacuation to Aizu-Wakamatsu, a new elementary and junior high school was opened there for Ōkuma children.

Ōita Prefecture is a prefecture in the Kyūshū region of Japan on the island of Kyūshū. The capital city is Ōita. Ōita is well known in Japan for its many hot springs. In the 6th century, one of the regions of Kyushu was divided into Bungo Province and Buzen Province. After the Meiji Restoration, districts from Bungo and Buzen provinces were combined to form Ōita Prefecture. 1184 (Juei 3): Usa Shrine was destroyed by fire in Gempei War. November 19, 1274 (Bun'ei 11, 20th day of the 10th month): Battle of Bun'ei August 15, 1281 (Kōan 4, 30th day of the 7th month): Battle of Kōan Ōita Prefecture is on the north-eastern section of the island of Kyūshū. Ōita is faces the Suo Channel and Honshū Island to the north. The prefecture looks towards the Iyo Channel and Shikoku Island to the east. It is bordered by Miyazaki Prefecture to the south. Fukuoka Prefecture and Kumamoto Prefecture are to the west. National Parks are established in about 28% of the total land area of the prefecture. Sasamuta-jinja, Usa-jinjū and Yusuhara Hachiman-gū are the chief Shinto shrines (ichinomiya) in the prefecture. Fukiji Temple has the oldest wooden structure in Kyushu. The Usuki Buddhas include 60+ cliff carvings from Heian period.

Ōsumi Province was an old province of Japan in the area of Kagoshima Prefecture on the island of Kyūshū. It was sometimes called Gūshū. Ōsumi had borders with Hyūga and Satsuma Provinces. The ancient capital city of the province was near Kokubu. In 713 (Wadō 6, 3rd month), the land of Ōsumi Province was separated from Hyūga. In the Meiji period, the provinces of Japan were converted into prefectures. Maps of Japan and Ōsumi Province were reformed in the 1870s. Japan's first satellite was named Ōsumi. It was launched February 11, 1970. Kagoshima jinja was the chief Shinto shrine (ichinomiya) of Ōsumi.

Ōmi Province is an old province of Japan in the area of Shiga Prefecture on the island of Honshū. It was also known as Gōshū. The ancient capital city of the province was near Ōtsu. Lake Biwa in Ōmi is Japan's largest lake. In the Kamakura period, Hōjō Tokimasa was made daimyo of Ōmi in 1200 (Shōji 2). In the Sengoku Period, the northern part of the province was the fief of Ishida Mitsunari. After the Battle of Sekigahara, Ōmi was controlled by the Ii clan who built the castle and town of Hikone. In the Edo period, the Tōkaidō road was the main route between the Imperial capital at Kyoto and the main city of the Tokugawa Shogunate. The road passed through Ōmi. Eight of the 69 Stations of the Nakasendō were in Ōmi. In the Meiji period, the provinces of Japan were converted into prefectures. The maps of Japan and Ōmi Province were reformed in the 1870s. Takebe taisha was the chief Shinto shrine (ichinomiya) of Ōmi. Enryaku-ji is one of the most important Buddhist centers. The monastery is on Mount Hiei (Hieizan).

Ōiso is a Japanese town in Kanagawa Prefecture on the island of Honshū. In the Edo period, Ōiso-juku was 8th of the 53 shogunate-maintained waystations (shuku-eki) along the Tōkaidō road which connected Edo and Kyoto. Ōiso is on the coastline of Sagami Bay.
Ōma is a town in Aomori, Japan. It is on the northernmost tip of Honshu. As of April 2012, the town has a population of about 6,240. Ōma is mainly a fishing town. The town is famous for its tuna.

Ōfunato is a city in southeastern Iwate, Japan. The city of Ōfunato was originally part of the ancient Mutsu Province. It has been settled since the Jōmon period. The modern village of Ōfunato was made within Kesen District, Iwate on April 1, 1889. In 1896, the Meiji-Sanriku earthquake caused a 25-meter tsunami that killed 27,000 people in Sanriku. Ōfunato was promoted officially promoted to town status on April 1, 1932. In 1933, a 8.4 magnitude earthquake stuck the town and caused a 28-meter tsunami that killed 1522 people. On April 1, 1952, the town of Sakari, and villages of Akasaki, Takkon, Massaki, Ikawa and Hikoroichi all merged with Ōfunato to form the city. On November 15, 2001, the town of Sanriku (from Kesen District) also merged into Ōfunato. Ōfunato was very badly damaged by the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami. The wave that hit the city was estimated to have reached 23.6 meters in height. It was listed that 3,498 out of 15,138 houses in the town were destroyed by the tsunami and 305 people were confirmed dead. At least six of Ōfunato's 58 designated evacuation sites were flooded by the tsunami.

Ōkato is a coastal town in the Taranaki Region of New Zealand's North Island. It is located on State Highway 45 and is 12 kilometers northeast of Ōakura and Warea 9 kilometers to the southwest. The town was established in the 1860s during the New Zealand Wars. It has a primary school in the town.

Ōkunoshima is a small island in the Inland Sea of Japan. It is sometimes called because there are a lot of rabbits on the island. Ōkunoshima played a big part in the Second Sino-Japanese War because it had a poison gas factory for Japan's chemical warfare in China.

Ōtemachi Station (大手町駅,おおてまちえき) is a railway station of Tokyo Metro and Toei Subway in Chiyoda, Tokyo, Japan. Ōtaki is a town in Isumi District, Chiba Prefecture, Japan. Ōtaki is at the middle of the Bōsō Peninsula. The town was the home of general Honda Tadakatsu during the Edo period (1603 – 1868). He built a large castle, Ōtaki Castle. The town had a population of about 10,412 (April 2012). The total area the town is 129.83 km². Ōtaki is at the center of the Bōsō Peninsula. Ōtaki has many hills, small mountains, and forestss. 70% of Ōtaki is covered by forest. Two rivers flow through the town: the Isumi River and the Yōrō River. Honda Tadakatsu built Ōtaki Castle on a hill in 1590. His samurai and many citizens built houses below the castle. The castle burned in 1842. A replica (copy) of the castle was built in 1975. A small museum is inside the castle. Japan National Route 297, to Ichihara or Tateyama Japan National Route 465, to Mobara or Futtsu

Ōtsu is a city in the Kansai region of Japan on the island of Honshu. It is the capital city of Shiga Prefecture. It has been recognized as a core city since 2009. Ōtsu was the site of an Imperial palace from 667 to 672. Emperor Tenji lived in Ōtsu. In the Edo period, Ōtsu was one of fifty-three shogunate-maintained waystations (shuku-eki) along the road which connected Edo and Kyoto. Ōtsu is on the south shore of Lake Biwa.
Şanlıurfa is a city in southeastern Turkey. The city is in the Southeastern Anatolia Region. In 2013, 1,801,980 people lived there. The city is mostly Arab and Kurdish as well as a minority of Turks.

Ōyamatsumi is a Mountain God in Shinto and the father of Ashinazuchi and Tenazuchi. He is also the father of Konohana Sakuya. His name ends with Mi which is an honorific particle used to express authority or divinity in Old Japanese.
Ōtorohanga is a town in the King Country, New Zealand. It is located 53 kilometers south of Hamilton and 18 kilometers north of Te Kūiti on State Highway 3. It is the home of the kiwi house.
Ōwhango is a small town in the Ruapehu District, New Zealand. It is 22 kilometers south of Taumarunui on State Highway 4. It has a primary school and is the home of rower Don Rowlands.

Şemdinli is a town located in the Şemdinli District of Hakkari Province in Turkey and had a population of 18,220 in 2023. The current mayor is Tahir Saklı from the Justice and Development Party (AKP), elected in 2019. The town is populated by Kurds of the Humaru and Zerzan tribes and moreover of mixed tribal and non-tribal origin. Its inhabitants are Sunni Muslims of the Shafi`i school. Şemdinli is divided into the five neighborhoods of Beşevler, Karşıyaka, Moda, Yayla and Yeni. A bomb exploded in Şemdinli town centre on November 1, 2005. It was officially attributed to the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), an armed Kurdish militant group. On November 9 one man was killed in a grenade attack on a local bookshop. The suspects of this attack, however, were caught in the act by bystanders. They were said to be members of a Turkish Gendarmerie unit, JITEM. The resulting investigation developed into a major political issue in Turkey in the first half of 2006. After a lengthy legal process the three suspects were eventually sentenced to 39 years in prison for being members of the PKK.
Şırnak is a city in southeastern Turkey. The city is in the Southeastern Anatolia Region. In 2020, 96,285 people lived there. The city is mainly populated by Kurds.
